section_summary: This section documents political, economic, and diplomatic developments in Japan between May and October 1940. It features Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's pivotal 'green telegram' series of September 12, 1940, advocating American firmness and potential force against Japanese expansion. Detailed embassy despatches analyze the dissolution of political parties, the transition from the Genro to the 'Jushin' consultative body, and the institutionalization and daily regimentation of Prince Konoye's totalitarian 'New National Structure'.

subfiles.about: Concluding section of a Peiping Embassy telegram reporting on regional political observations.
subfiles.summary: Final page of Peiping telegram No. 300 (section 6), distributed to the State Department, Chungking and Shanghai, coded text by airmail to Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 300 from Peiping (Section 6)

subfiles.about: Reporting the appointment of Admiral Koshiro Oikawa as Navy Minister.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Admiral Koshiro Oikawa appointed Navy Minister succeeding Yoshida; he was Commander-in-Chief at Yokosuka.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 800: Appointment of Navy Minister

subfiles.about: Administrative charge slip tracking file 894.00 and cross-referenced papers.
subfiles.summary: Internal State Department charge slip routing file 894.00/954-1/2 and tracking related documentation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip

subfiles.about: Personal letter describing rationing, inflation, and shortages in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Blakemore writes from Shibuya, Tokyo, detailing the rising cost of living, rampant illicit trading, and acute shortages of fuel, leather, coffee, and butter. He describes the introduction of rationing for sugar and matches, military profit controls, and a severe water shortage affecting several wards of Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Tom Blakemore on Economic Conditions and Shortages in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Informal letter discussing social life, Prince Chichibu, and the hazards of speaking Japanese.
subfiles.summary: Blakemore describes attending the annual dinner of the Cambridge-Oxford Society and conversing with Prince Chichibu, noting the prince's English and public role. He reflects on diplomatic language protocol and explains his decision to avoid Japanese in delicate matters, citing Ambassador Grew's prudent example.
subfiles.title: Letter from Tom Blakemore on Meeting Prince Chichibu and Language Caution

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for telegram 528 on Cabinet crisis and Foreign Minister's speech.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Tokyo telegram No. 528 (July 2, 1940): political situation, possible cabinet crisis, and aftermath of Arita's radio speech.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note: Political Situation and Cabinet Crisis

subfiles.about: Strategic assessment evaluating A. T. Steele's views and advocating a firm American policy.
subfiles.summary: Grew reviews A. T. Steele's thesis that firmness is the safest course: conciliation has passed since Yonai fell, and Anglo-American solidarity and naval expansion are inducing caution in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 827: Strategic Review of U.S.-Japan Policy (Sections 1-4)

subfiles.about: Analysis of risks associated with economic embargoes and the necessity of resisting aggression.
subfiles.summary: Grew discusses high-pressure Japanese diplomacy in the Netherlands East Indies and Indochina. He weighs the risks that drastic petroleum embargoes might provoke rash retaliation by military elements against the far greater dangers of a laissez-faire policy toward totalitarian aggression.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 828: Strategic Review of U.S.-Japan Policy (Sections 5-7)

subfiles.about: Argument for maintaining the Pacific status quo and utilizing force or display of force.
subfiles.summary: Grew warns that Japan has become predatory and opportunistic, presenting a direct threat to American and British interests. He argues that American security depends on British survival and that only a determined show of force can preserve the Pacific status quo until Britain prevails in Europe.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 829: Strategic Review of U.S.-Japan Policy (Section 7 cont.)

subfiles.about: Specific policy recommendations regarding Shanghai and embassy staff consensus.
subfiles.summary: Grew endorses Department instructions on the Shanghai defense sectors and advocates progressive reciprocal adjustments in relations. He concludes that unyielding patience has become dangerous and notes the full concurrence of his military, naval, and commercial attaches.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 830: Strategic Review of U.S.-Japan Policy (Sections 8-9)

subfiles.about: State Department commendation of Grew's comprehensive policy analysis.
subfiles.summary: Department thanks Grew for the penetrating analysis in telegram No. 827.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram No. 364 to Tokyo

subfiles.about: Clarification that Grew's analysis was independently formed and uninfluenced by Lord Lothian.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports reading a telegram detailing Lord Lothian's conversations in Washington and emphasizes that the remarkable alignment between their views was entirely fortuitous and reached independently.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 834: Independence of Views from Lord Lothian

subfiles.about: Report on high-level Imperial audiences and extraordinary Cabinet meeting.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports unusual Imperial audiences for Princes Kanin and Fushimi and Matsuoka, and an extraordinary Cabinet meeting.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 845: Unusual Political and Imperial Conferences

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing telegram 864 regarding friction in establishing the new structure.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference for telegram No. 864: building the New Structure in Japan is not proceeding smoothly.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note: Friction in New Structure Movement

subfiles.about: Division summary of Despatch 4917 concerning the replacement of the Genro by the Jushin.
subfiles.summary: State Department summary of Tokyo despatch No. 4917, detailing how the traditional elder statesmen advisory role held by Prince Saionji has been replaced by the 'Jushin' council of former premiers and dignitaries.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Summary of Despatch No. 4917: Japan's New Genro

subfiles.about: Detailed historical analysis of the transition from the Genro to the Jushin council.
subfiles.summary: Embassy despatch reviewing the decline of party cabinets following the 1932 assassinations and Prince Saionji's diminished influence. It details the emergence of the 'Jushin'—comprising the Lord Privy Seal, Privy Council President, and former premiers—as a permanent consultative council better aligned with Japanese paternalist traditions.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 4917: Japan's New Genro

subfiles.about: Division summary of Despatch 4928 on the widespread use of the term 'New Structure'.
subfiles.summary: Summary: the phrase 'New Structure' is applied to explain countless restrictions and economies in private life.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Summary of Despatch No. 4928: Comments on the New Structure

subfiles.about: Report on the popular reception and social manifestations of the 'New Structure'.
subfiles.summary: Grew examines how Prince Konoye's New Structure movement operates as an economic and cultural transformation characterized by traditionalism and anti-foreignism. A comprehensive survey of August press headlines illustrates widespread regimentation, including bans on jazz, dancehalls, foreign school directors, and luxury items.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 4928: Comments on the 'New Structure'

subfiles.about: Division summary of Despatch 4946 analyzing the origins, principles, and nature of the New National Structure.
subfiles.summary: Summary analyzing Prince Konoye's movement to unify national power and eliminate party politics, noting military collaboration and comparing the structure to European fascism modified by Japanese traditions.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Summary of Despatch No. 4946: The New National Structure

subfiles.about: In-depth political report tracing the history, ideology, and organizational plans of the New National Structure.
subfiles.summary: Grew delivers a comprehensive study of the movement to abolish parliamentary factionalism and unify national life under Imperial assistance. He recounts the dissolution of political parties, analyzes the delicate relationship between the Cabinet and the military Supreme Command, examines the nationalist membership of the Preparatory Committee, and predicts an indigenous form of totalitarianism without personal dictatorship.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 4946: The 'New National Structure' in Japan

subfiles.about: Official translation of Prince Konoye's address establishing the New National Structure.
subfiles.summary: Premier Konoye outlines the philosophical foundation of the New National Structure to the Preparatory Committee. He stresses that the movement is not a political party or single-party dictatorship, but a permanent, all-encompassing national organization enabling all subjects to fulfill their duty of assisting the Throne.
subfiles.title: Address by Prime Minister Prince Fumimaro Konoye to the Preparatory Committee
subfiles.to: Preparatory Committee for the New National Structure

subfiles.about: Reporting Konoye's denial of communistic tendencies within the New National Structure.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Konoye's denial of communist ideas in the New National Structure, with Asahi and Nichi Nichi reactions.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 957: Konoye's Denial of Communistic Tendencies

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding Treasury Agent interview with Vice Minister Hiroshi Kondo.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Treasury letter enclosing a resume of Vice Minister Kondo's interview with a Treasury Agent.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note: Interview with Vice Minister Kondo

subfiles.about: Division summary of Despatch 5037 describing press reflections of rapid social regimentation.
subfiles.summary: State Department summary describing Tokyo despatch No. 5037, highlighting the regimentation of daily Japanese life and listing illustrative press headlines regarding dress, transport, and organizations.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Summary of Despatch No. 5037: The New Structure in the Headlines

subfiles.about: Despatch describing the grim atmosphere, suspicion of foreigners, and press headlines under the New Structure.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports on the grim transformation of Japanese society, marked by pervasive police suspicion, hostility toward foreigners, and the replacement of genial diplomats by rigid officials. He begins an extensive recitation of September press headlines illustrating comprehensive regimentation.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 5037: The 'New Structure' in the Headlines
